opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Donna Ball (E024) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is within the allowed maximum (up to write; admin would require owning role). Requested level equals the maximum, so granting write is appropriate.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: IT DB confirms Donna Ball (E024) is a Payroll Specialist, full-time per HR. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning role (Engineer for Source Code), which doesn't apply. Requested level equals the maximum, so recommending write.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Donna Ball (E024) is a Payroll Specialist, full-time per HR. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the system (Engineer for Source Code), which doesn't apply here. Requested level equals the maximum, so granting write is appropriate.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Donna Ball (E024) is a Payroll Specialist; full-time per HR. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the system (Engineer for Source Code), which does not apply. Requested level equals the maximum, so granting write is appropriate.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Donna Ball (E024) is a Payroll Specialist; full-time per HR. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the system (Engineer for Source Code), which does not apply. Requested level equals the maximum, so recommending write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Donna Ball (E024) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum allowed is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommending read.
reason: Donna Ball (E024) requested write access to Source Code. Most agents report her as a full-time Payroll Specialist (max write), but the Security agent's DB shows she is a contractor with only basic security training. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps the maximum at read. Since the requested write level exceeds read, the maximum (read) is granted. No admin is ever allowed for contractors, and Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code.

The team memory has 6 notes. Five agents (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say she is a full-time Payroll Specialist and recommend write. The Security agent says she is a contractor with basic security training and recommends read.

There's a conflict: HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities say full-time; Security says contractor.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Donna is a Payroll Specialist, not Engineer.

If full-time: max is write. Requested write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write → grant read.

So the decision hinges on employment type. Majority (5 notes) say full-time, Security says contractor. Which to trust? The Security agent note might be more specialized for this. Hmm.

Typically in these tasks, one agent may have a conflicting fact. We need to decide based on evidence. The Security agent's note says "Security DB shows Donna Ball (E024) is a contractor with basic security training." HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities all confirm full-time per HR.

Actually, let me think about which is more reliable. The HR agent is the source of employment type typically. Five agents corroborate full-time. One agent (Security) says contractor. But Security agent is also the one who knows security training.

Hmm, this is a classic discrepancy. The majority says full-time. But the Security agent has specific info about security training, which suggests the Security DB has her as contractor.
